st: Put the octopus in a pot with [[2 cups]] water and a pinch of the salt. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes until it starts to soften.
Drain the octopus, saving the cooking liquid.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute. Stir in the curry powder and turmeric and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and thyme and cook 5 minutes until they break down.
Add the octopus, the coconut milk, [[1 cup]] of the saved liquid and the remaining salt.
Simmer gently, partly covered, for 35 minutes until the octopus is tender and the sauce is thick. Add more liquid if it dries out.
While it cooks, cook the rice according to the package directions.
Taste and adjust the salt, then serve over the rice.

ing: such as tuna, kingfish or snapper, in large chunks
st: Toss the fish with the lime juice, turmeric and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Let it sit for 10 minutes.
Start cooking the rice according to the package directions.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute. Stir in the curry powder for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until soft and saucy.
Pour in the coconut milk, the water and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Lay in the fish. Cover and simmer very gently for 8 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily (145°F/63°C).
Taste and adjust the salt and serve over rice.

ing: shark steak or firm white fish
st: Bring [[3 cups]] water and half the salt to a boil in a pot.
Add the shark and simmer for 10 minutes until cooked through (145°F/63°C).
Drain and cool. Remove any skin and bones, then mash the fish with a fork until finely flaked.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, chili and turmeric and stir for 1 minute.
Add the sliced bilimbi or mango and the lime juice. Cook for 5 minutes until soft and sour.
Stir in the mashed fish and the remaining salt. Cook for 8 minutes, mashing and stirring until it forms a thick, dry-ish chutney.
Serve warm or at room temperature with rice or as a filling for bread.

ing: such as bok choy, spinach or amaranth leaves, loosely packed
st: Wash the greens well and chop them roughly.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, garlic and ginger for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and thyme and cook for 4 minutes.
Pour in [[5 cups]] water and add the salt. Bring to a boil.
Add the fish, reduce the heat and simmer gently for 6 minutes until just cooked (145°F/63°C).
Add the greens and simmer for 5 minutes until tender.
Season with pepper, taste and adjust the salt. Serve hot as a light soup or over rice.
Pat the fish dry. Make three diagonal cuts on each side through the skin to the bone.
Mash the garlic, ginger, chili, salt, pepper and turmeric with [[2 tbsp]] oil and the lime juice to make a paste.
Rub the paste over the fish and inside the cuts and belly. Marinate for 30 minutes in the refrigerator.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high, and brush the grates with the remaining [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Grill the fish for 7 minutes on the first side without moving it, so the skin does not stick.
Flip carefully and grill for 6 minutes more, until the flesh is opaque and reaches 145°F/63°C.
Serve with lime wedges, rice and a green salad.
Combine the sweet potatoes, water and cinnamon stick in a pot. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 10 minutes until the sweet potatoes begin to soften.
Add the plantains, sugar and salt. Stir gently to dissolve the sugar.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered over low heat for 25 minutes, stirring carefully, until the fruit and potatoes are soft and the sauce is syrupy.
Stir in the nutmeg and vanilla and remove the cinnamon stick.
Serve warm or chilled, in bowls, with some sauce spooned over.
Rub a little oil on your hands and peel the green bananas with a knife. Cut into chunks and keep in cold water so they do not darken.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, ginger and thyme for 1 minute.
Drain the bananas and add them to the pot with [[2 cups]] water and the salt.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the bananas are nearly tender.
Add the fish and the coconut milk. Stir gently.
Simmer uncovered for 12 minutes, until the fish is cooked through (145°F/63°C) and the bananas are soft and the sauce thick.
Taste and adjust the salt, remove the thyme stems, and serve hot.

ing: fresh, or one can drained, sliced into rounds
st: If using canned hearts of palm, drain and rinse them well. Pat dry.
Slice the hearts of palm into thin rounds or ribbons.
Soak the sliced onion in cold water for 5 minutes to mellow its bite, then drain.
Whisk the lime juice, oil, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Add the palm hearts, onion, chili and tomato. Toss gently.
Let the salad stand for 10 minutes so the flavors blend.
Sprinkle with cilantro and serve cold.
